answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may place work offers. A sparrow account with no stake cannot multiply into influence: an attacker creating thousands of identities must fund every one, and provable double-signing or abandoned jobs can forfeit the deposits. The beacon is the public rule that triggers slashing, so honest agents can verify penalties. Using copper as the deposit asset makes the cost concrete: capital is tied up and exposed to loss, not merely spent on cheap account creation.
